Worst birthday experience ever.

Despite booking and paying in advance for a table and a bowling alley, we faced constant pushing and overcrowding (dhakka-mukki) throughout the evening. I raised the issue multiple times in advance with both the lady and male bouncers, yet every complaint was ignored.

Shockingly, one bouncer was openly encouraging other people to play for free on our paid bowling lane. PR staff casually brought their girlfriends to our table and bowling area, and one PR even took drinks from our table without permission.

To make matters worse, a man wearing a sleeveless vest (sando) — clearly allowed by this “sando-only club of Mumbai” — used extremely abusive and vulgar language, including offensive remarks involving mothers. What is most disturbing is that PRs, bouncers, and even one of the owners present at the time witnessed everything and chose to do nothing. They simply stood there and watched.

Let’s be honest — if such language had been used toward your sister or girlfriend, it would never have been tolerated. Stand for the truth.

The environment felt unsafe, unprofessional, and deeply disrespectful, especially for paying guests celebrating a private occasion. My birthday was completely ruined, and I will never recommend this place.

Public note:
Next time, boys and men — please wear sandos (ganjis) 😍
Apparently, this is the only club in Mumbai that proudly entertains men in innerwear 🤣🤣🤣🤣

Despite all this, there was not even a single apology. The PR (J*Y), who was never present to check on guest safety or comfort, suddenly appeared at billing time demanding cash.

PR J*Y and the owner present that night — after witnessing the abuse and repeated complaints, no one took a stand for the truth.

featured_reviews.name: Jay Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ 1 Star

Extremely disappointing experience at Game Palacio Bandra. We booked a table for 8 people on a Saturday night by paying an advance amount through their PR, Jay, who assured us that we would get a bowling lane at 10:30 PM and specifically asked us to arrive accordingly. We reached at 10:35 PM—just 5 minutes late—and despite informing him and paying in advance, he told us that our lane had already been given away and that they could no longer assure us anything. This completely ruined our plans.

The worst part was that Jay made promises just to sell us the table and then failed to honor any of his commitments. We were willing to wait and stayed until closing time, but nobody followed up with us regarding bowling or provided any proper resolution.

There was also no prior communication that table service was restricted to bottle purchases only. After spending nearly ₹25,000, we were given a cramped table under the staircase where our heads were literally touching the stairs. Only after repeatedly requesting the manager and PR were we allowed to order beers and cocktails.

To make matters worse, a service charge of nearly ₹3,000 was added to the bill and was not removed despite multiple requests. We were incorrectly told it was mandatory, which is not in line with current government guidelines regarding service charges.

The venue also shut around 1:10 AM despite being told it would remain open until at least 1:30 AM. Overall, terrible customer service, false commitments, poor management, and a complete waste of a Saturday night. There are far better places in Bandra to spend your money. Game Palacio should be your last choice.

Smaaash Lower Parel — Still Brings Out My Inner Child
I’ve been visiting Smaaash Lower Parel for more than a decade, and it’s one of those rare places that has managed to grow with time without losing its core charm.
Back in the day, it was all about adult-oriented fun — late nights, high energy, friends, and honestly, partying like an animal. The go-karting, especially at night, has always been a personal favourite, along with the bowling arenas, cricket box, and a wide mix of adrenaline-packed games that made it a go-to hangout spot.

Fun fact: I’ve literally celebrated every phase of life here — I even had a breakup party at Smaaash in 2014, which somehow makes my bond with this place even stronger 😄.

What I really appreciate now is how Smaaash has evolved over time. Initially, the focus was clearly more on adults, but lately they’ve done a great job of introducing kid-friendly games without taking away the excitement that adults come for.
Last night felt like a full-circle moment. I visited with my 11-year-old nephew and 7-year-old niece, and they absolutely loved it. From the games to the overall vibe, they were completely engaged and having a blast. Seeing the same place work just as well for kids today as it once did for us adults was genuinely satisfying.
Smaaash still does what it’s always done best ,it brings out your inner child, no matter your age. And now, with the younger generation hooked, I’m pretty sure I’ll be coming here regularly again.
A place full of memories, that adapts with time and still delivers fun... Smaaash Lower Parel continues to hit the mark.

We discovered YEY Yaya Kids Club while we were in Bombay for shopping. My wife and I had our little one with us and he was getting bored, so we decided to try this place for about 1.5 hours (₹650) and honestly, it was completely worth every rupee.

The place is very well equipped and thoughtfully designed for kids. Right from the moment you enter, there’s so much for them to explore, trampoline, slides, climbing wall, crazy cars, a kids’ supermarket, kids’ salon, and even that fun bulldozer game where kids pick up balls like mud and slide down. They also have a big indoor play area, in-house café, and even paid games for extra fun. The space is clean, safe, colourful and very well managed. You can also host birthday parties here which we noticed a lot of parents doing, it’s a perfect setup for that.

What I really liked is that it gives parents a break while kids are happily engaged in a proper play environment. For us, it turned a tiring shopping day into a smooth one because our kid came out smiling and exhausted in the best way 😄

featured_reviews.name: Gerry Savage
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited on a weekday (Wednesday) but were charged the weekend entry price without any prior notice. It was not a government or national holiday. After being charged, I noticed the bill listed a weekend rate, and when I questioned it, I was told it was because of Pongal (which is not a national holiday). There were no signs, notices, or verbal mention before payment that weekend pricing would apply.
There are excessive restrictions throughout the facility (what children can do, what they can play with, and even how they’re allowed to play). In the pretend play area, costumes are not allowed to be removed from the spot and are only permitted for photos. My child was asked to remove a costume, yet there is no signage explaining this rule. If the area is for photos only, that should be clearly stated.
In the arcade, you only get one play. Several amenities were also not functioning, including the crane game and the rock-climbing area. Other areas were taped up, torn, or visibly run down, making the place feel poorly maintained and potentially unsafe.
There are also rules about where adults are allowed, but no clear indication of which areas are restricted. Overall, the staff managed the space in a very stern manner, which is not appropriate for a children’s play area.
Between the misleading weekday pricing, excessive and unclear rules, broken attractions, and poor maintenance, the experience was extremely disappointing. What was supposed to be a fun outing for my three-year-old turned into a frustrating and unpleasant experience. At best, the practices feel dishonest.

The focus seems more on commercial aspects rather than providing a genuine play area for kids.

featured_reviews.review_text: We came here after watching reels to let the kids enjoy the ball pool, but it was a very bad experience. The staff was not cooperative at all, and they were not even allowing my 13-month-old baby to play for 5min . The place is not fresh or well-maintained, and the environment feels very dark and dull. I would suggest not visiting this place just by watching paid reels — please read genuine reviews before coming.

featured_reviews.name: Syed Hadi
featured_reviews.review_text: Good place to spend some time with your friends or kids, it is too bowling. All is and rage room as well as a small trampoline park which includes the ball pit. There are also basic games The overall pricing is good and the facilities are average. However, the location is very good so it is a recommended place affair in the area and have some time to spend.

featured_reviews.name: gaurav vaikul
featured_reviews.review_text: Worst its not what you see in reel my 13month infant was charged full amount for the trampoline and ball pool section and when I asked where it’s written that Infant will be charged as full adult they simply don’t have answer pls stay away

featured_reviews.name: Akash Saindane
featured_reviews.review_text: Very disappointing experience at Rush Trampoline Park. We visited after watching Instagram reels and expected much more, but the actual experience was not up to the mark. Activities were very limited and it mostly felt like just a ball pool setup. Considering the overall experience, the pricing is too high and not worth the money. Management and coordination also need improvement. Would not recommend based on our experience.

featured_reviews.name: Saonli Roy
featured_reviews.review_text: This indoor play area is nicely decorated and clean. My kid enjoy a lot, it was hard to bring him back. Price is actually high, for 1 hour they charged 600 ₹. Additional 30 min, 300 ₹. That is too too much, I did not find it justified. So i only kept my kid for 1 h.

featured_reviews.name: Abhigyan Bafna
featured_reviews.review_text:
The wreaking room was okay. But what ruined the experience was Bowling.

The bowling here uses old string tech which causes errors, long wait times and wrong fouls. The way they get you is that the price for it is 600 for 2. But not worth it. Can go for  rage room as an experience.

featured_reviews.name: Jayesh Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: Never go to this place. AC was off there were mosquitos flying over there. In bowling the pins are tied with ropes and if you trying to strike in bowling it is impossible. Bowling ball does not come out of machine you have to put hand in the machine and remove it. Their staff was just standing and not even helped even after asked. Pathetic

featured_reviews.review_text: Best places for kids for enjoying the day per kids its 750/- and carry socks for play area if you don't have there will be charged for 100/- per pair . We went on sunday it was not crowded. Beautiful ambience and great lemon juice and french fries.
